findings.title: Optimized paginator cannot paginate datetime-ordered audit logs
findings.body: `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` applies `math.floor`/`math.ceil` directly to the ordered field value. The audit-log endpoint selects this paginator with `order_by="-datetime"`, so each result has a `datetime` value and cursor construction raises `TypeError` on the first optimized request. Unlike `DateTimePaginator`, this class neither converts datetimes to a numeric cursor value nor converts cursor values back to datetimes for the ranged query. Consequently, an administrator requesting `optimized_pagination=true` receives a 500 rather than audit-log results.

findings.title: Advanced negative-offset path uses unsupported Django queryset slicing
findings.body: The new advanced path passes a negative `start_offset` directly to `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing or slicing and raise an error rather than interpreting it as reverse/boundary pagination. Cursor parsing accepts negative offsets (`Cursor.from_string` converts the offset with `int`), so an authorized caller can cause the optimized audit-log endpoint to return a 500 with a cursor such as `0:-1:0`; the advertised reverse-pagination feature is not functional.
